title: Groove rings without the V key: in crease mode a normal ring-tool click drafts the groove ring
description: User 2026-10-08 on CRAW-60: the V key (draft a ring along the groove at the cursor) does not make sense as a separate gesture. Instead the ring tool's mode (T cycles geodesic / crease, and CRAW-31's field modes if landed) decides what a normal click drafts: in crease mode the hover preview and the click draft are the groove ring (AuthoredSplineRing.traceGroove), in geodesic mode today's plane ring. Remove the V key and its control hint.
definition-of-done: 1. V removed. 2. T sets the mode for the next draft as well as the open draft; the hover preview follows the mode and is drawn in the mode's colour (geodesic red, crease purple, named Color constants). 3. Crease mode previews and drafts a ring wherever geodesic mode would: its one authored anchor is the cursor vertex, on the same girdling plane the geodesic preview uses; only the rest of the loop is pulled into grooves by the crease cost. No groove reach, no in-groove threshold, no groove-share gate, no climb to the groove bottom, no switch to the groove's own plane, no "% in groove" readout or colour fade. 4. Crease mode never drafts a geodesic ring; the hover is what a click commits. A crease ring never crosses itself: its two halves leave the cursor anchor by different first vertices and the walk is loop-erased (GrooveRingBenchmark#crossingsOverManyCursorVertices: crease crossings 0.3% of 401 crawfish vertices); the hover shows only simple rings and the first click refuses a self-crossing one. 5. Mode survives confirm, reopen, undo, save; a crease ring saves and reloads through mode="crease". 6. Code left dead by 3 deleted. 7. Tests updated. 8. Crease hover timed on the crawfish copy against the geodesic hover.
testing-plan: CreaseRingTest updated for click-in-crease-mode; live on a crawfish copy.
changes-made: V removed. RingTool.newDraftMode is the mode a click drafts in; T flips it (and the open draft's, as one undoable edit, when a draft is open), the hint shows the open draft's mode or else the next one. Undo/redo, confirm, re-open and Ctrl+S leave newDraftMode alone; a confirmed ring keeps its own mode through re-open, undo and save as in CRAW-60. Click in crease mode: AuthoredSplineRing.traceGroove at the clicked vertex on the girdling plane (one undoable 'groove ring drafted'); a refused groove drafts the plane ring in geodesic mode with lastError 'groove ring refused, drafted the plane ring: <reason>' (logged; ui-state error), newDraftMode stays crease. Hover in crease mode: the full groove trace measured 250-2200 ms per hover on IMG_4109 in the scene (vs 60-130 ms for the geodesic hover), too slow, so the preview is the plane ring through the bottom of the groove the click will ring, on that groove's own plane (120-260 ms, or the plane ring at the cursor with ui-state previewGrooveRefusal when no groove is in reach); only the click traces the crease path (59 ms on the carapace groove, 98% in the groove). traceGroove's groove search is split out as AuthoredSplineRing.nearestGroove (callers: traceGroove, the hover). Test GL proxy FontGlStandIn moved to unit.GlStandIn and shared. CreaseRingTest: hover shows the notch's groove and the click rings that same groove in the notch, T switches draft and next mode, confirm/re-open/undo keep both; refused groove on a plain tube drafts the plane ring and says why. Full mvn test 457/0. Verification: launch entry 'CRAW-63: groove rings by click in crease mode (crawfish copy)', screenshots tmp/craw63-crease-hover-preview(-crop).png and tmp/craw63-crease-click-groove-ring(-crop).png; Enter + Ctrl+S wrote mode="crease" with surface_creases (kept as tmp/crawfish_rings.with-groove-ring.dsl, launch copy restored).

Follow-up after the user found crease mode indistinguishable from geodesic. (a) Colour tells the mode: RingTool.GEODESIC_DRAFT_COLOR = Color.RED and CREASE_DRAFT_COLOR = Color.BRIGHT_PURPLE (new constant) colour the preview, the draft and a ring a click would re-open (by its own mode); Color.toPackedRgb converts for the overlay; PREVIEW_COLOR removed; the lavender 0x9D7BFF in RING_COLORS became teal 0x3DE8C8 so no confirmed ring reads as a crease draft. (b) No fallback: the crease hover runs AuthoredSplineRing.traceGroove itself (same vertex, same girdling plane as the click; only the final depth differs, as in geodesic mode), so with no groove in reach previewValid is false and nothing is drawn; a click then drafts nothing. The plane-ring stand-in preview, previewGrooveRefusal, nearestGroove and the 'drafted the plane ring' fallback are gone (the superseded entry above describes them). (c) Speed: the sheet Dijkstra now runs on SurfaceGeodesics' primitive heap (heapKey/heapVertex/heapSize, heapPush/heapPop made public, no third heap copy; MESH-56 unifies), walks the SurfaceMetric flat half-edge arrays instead of the mesh's per-vertex edge lists, and for a one-anchor ring stops where the search meets its own sheet-swapped mirror (half the ring's cost) instead of running to the far sheet; traceGroove's reach queue is a reused field. Timings, IMG_4109 crawfish copy, same 9 groove points: before (PriorityQueue<double[]>, mesh lists, full search) a crease trace took median 196 ms / max 325 ms, of which ~70% Dijkstra (PriorityQueue.poll 26%, mesh adjacency 25%, loop body) and ~29% spline fit; after: crease hover median 69 ms / max 184 ms (click draft 74/185 ms), ~33% Dijkstra (~22 ms) and ~65% SplineAnchorFit.fit (~45 ms: insertAnchor 50%, setAnchors 33%, scanDeviation 15%), groove search + plane loop ~1%. Geodesic hover at the same points: median 18 ms / max 101 ms (all 28 valid geodesic points: median 12 ms). Remaining gap: the crease Dijkstra is work geodesic mode does not do, and the fit costs more because the groove reference is a jagged vertex path needing more supporting anchors (e.g. 21 vs ~11); neither is a hard limit (a narrower search slab or smoothing the reference before fitting could cut them) but both change results, so left for MESH-56 / a follow-up. CreaseRingTest: crease hover is the groove ring and the click rings the same groove; on a plain tube crease mode previews nothing and the click drafts nothing, newDraftMode stays crease. Screenshots tmp/craw63-geodesic-preview-red(-crop).png, tmp/craw63-crease-preview-purple(-crop).png, tmp/craw63-crease-no-groove-nothing(-crop).png, tmp/craw63-crease-draft-purple(-crop).png; sweep data tmp/geodesic-final.jsonl, tmp/crease-final.jsonl, profile tmp/profile-final.html.

wt done synced onto master f785f696 (VIEW-20 refusal toasts): RingTool conflicts resolved by keeping refusalShown round T and the click's errorToasts call, dropping master's V key; the click's 'no preview' refusal now names the red/purple preview of the current mode instead of 'pink'. Full mvn test after the sync 482/0.

Predictable crease placement (user: "can't tell where it will pop up"). Crease mode now previews and drafts the ring wherever geodesic mode would: the one authored anchor is the cursor vertex, on the girdling plane the geodesic preview uses (previewPlaneNormal); only the rest of the loop is pulled into grooves by the crease cost (the existing CREASE-mode AuthoredSplineRing.trace). Hover and click both call previewRing/draftRing.trace with mode = newDraftMode, so the click path is one branch for both modes (undo name 'draft opened', report 'drafted'); no '% in groove' text, no colour fade. The opening click no longer refuses a ring that crosses itself (keepSimple false there; the report row names the crossing), because on the crawfish the purple preview at a carapace point was refused on click for crossing itself, breaking hover = click. Deleted: AuthoredSplineRing.traceGroove (reach BFS, climb to the groove bottom, groove-plane-then-girdle retry, refusal text), GROOVE_REACH_OF_RADIUS, IN_GROOVE_STRENGTH, MINIMUM_GROOVE_FRACTION, PERCENT, grooveFraction and its per-trace computation, grooveNormal, reachQueue, clickPosition; SurfaceCreases.acrossGroove with its tensor diffusion and power iteration (CHANNELS, POWER_ITERATIONS) and the constructor's acrossGroove parameter (valleyStrength/edgeCost unchanged: the scalar channel diffused independently before). GrooveRingBenchmark: candidate rows now trace the crease ring at the click on the hover's plane; the across-groove arrays are gone. CreaseRingTest: crease ring anchored at the click on the click's plane and lying in the notch while the geodesic cuts across; crease statement round-trip (mode="crease", normal = the click's plane); tool hover/click through the cursor with the same plane, T/confirm/re-open/undo keep modes; on a plain tube crease mode previews and drafts through the cursor in crease mode; a ridge does not attract the crease ring. Hover timing, IMG_4109 crawfish copy, 63-point grid (tmp/geodesic-cursor.jsonl, tmp/crease-cursor.jsonl): crease preview valid at exactly the 28 points geodesic is; at those points geodesic median 12 ms / max 98 ms, crease median 17 ms / max 110 ms. Open: at both screenshot points the crease ring drafts but crosses itself (named in the row; the geodesic ring at the claw point is simple), so the crease fit through one cursor anchor can loop; left for MESH-56 / a follow-up. Full mvn test 481/0 (one fewer than before: the plain-tube refusal test was folded into the smooth-stretch tool test). Screenshots: tmp/craw63-crease-cursor-groove(-crop).png, tmp/craw63-crease-cursor-groove-hover-crop.png, tmp/craw63-crease-cursor-smooth(-crop).png. Launch entry renamed 'CRAW-63: crease rings through the cursor by click in crease mode (crawfish copy)'.

Crease rings crossing themselves (follow-up). Measured with GrooveRingBenchmark#crossingsOverManyCursorVertices (new, kept): 401 IMG_4109 crawfish-copy vertices (every 1172nd of 469131), each on its girdling plane as the hover finds it, geodesic and crease traced at full depth. Before: geodesic 7/400 crossing (1.8%), crease 198/401 (49.4%), mean in-groove length (fraction of ring length with valley strength >= 0.5 at both ends) crease 0.503, geodesic 0.139. Classification of the 198 crossing crease rings: (A) spur at the cursor 198, (B) loop elsewhere 0, (C) simple walk but the fit crosses 0; 250 walks revisited a vertex. Groove discount alone does not help: GROOVE_COST_OF_LENGTH 0.05/0.2/0.35/0.5/0.7 gave 49.4/48.4/47.4/45.9/46.1% crossing (all spurs) while in-groove fell 0.503 -> 0.309. Fix 1 (spur): the meet-in-the-middle only accepts a meeting whose two halves leave the anchor by different first vertices (AuthoredSplineRing.sheetBranch, a primitive per-state field holding each state's first step from the source): 70/401 crossing (17.5%), all now loop-elsewhere (halves sharing a vertex on opposite sheets), in-groove 0.541. Fix 2 (loop erasure): the walk is laid down chronologically loop-erased (a revisit pops back to the earlier visit, never past an authored anchor; scratch is the searches' own sheetVisit/sheetParent under a fresh stamp): 1/400 crossing (0.3%, a fit crossing), in-groove 0.527, crease mean 34 ms / worst 302 ms vs geodesic 32/282 ms in the benchmark. Loop erasure without fix 1 collapses the spur rings: only 151/401 traced. So the plane-tie step (slab / discount / plane cost) and the angle-monotone seam were not needed; CREASE_BAND_OF_RADIUS stays 1.0, GROOVE_COST_OF_LENGTH stays 0.05. First click: the refusal of a self-crossing ring is restored (retraceDraft(..., true) as on master), and the hover no longer offers a ring that crosses itself (previewAt returns previewRing.simple), so hover and click agree except where the full-depth click trace crosses and the one-level-shallower preview did not. CreaseRingTest.creaseRingsBesideTheNotchNeverRunOutAndBackAlongAStem clicks 12 sides x 31 offsets round the notched tube; with both fixes disabled 120-odd of those rings crossed (scan), with them all are simple. Full mvn test 482/0. Not yet done: live hover timing in the scene, refreshed screenshots under tmp/, wt done.
Correction to the entry above: with both fixes disabled the tube scan had 98 of 372 crease rings crossing (not 120-odd).
